DentalPULSE · Atria research · Nov 10

20 static formats we haven’t run yet

Most of our recent statics share one layout: a headline in the top left and the Pod below it. Each card here shows a format that is running now in health and beauty, why it stops the scroll, and how it would look for DentalPULSE.

How these were picked
  • Atria library: active static image ads launched since Aug 15 in health, beauty and personal care, sorted by impressions
  • Searched by format, not product: post-it notes, negative marketing, statistics, quiz, interface, press, quote, question, before/after, comparison
  • Plus Atria’s hand-picked template set
  • 126 ads reviewed. Dropped formats we already use and any built on cartoons, memes or award badges.

Scroll-stoppers with no product in the frame

Real objects and raw photos. The product appears in the primary text or the last frame, so nothing in the feed reads as an ad.

01 Dr. Richard Calloway · 74 days running

Lawn sign statement

A real yard sign carries one blunt sentence. It reads like news from the neighborhood, not a brand.

DentalPULSE version

A printed lawn sign in a front yard: “YOUR DENTURES AREN’T OLD. THEY’RE DIRTY.”

DenturesTop of funnel

02 Dr. Annie Gonzalez · 19 days running

Marker on the real thing

Handwriting drawn straight onto the subject (a neck) with a warning and an arrow pointing down to the answer.

DentalPULSE version

Dry-erase marker on a bathroom mirror, over the reflection of a woman holding up her yellowed denture: “Do NOT buy another box of tablets. Here’s what actually works ↓”

DenturesTop of funnel

03 Stasis · 10 days, new

Wall-of-text plea

Hot-pink field, all text, first person, urgent. Looks nothing like a product ad and gets read to the end.

DentalPULSE version

“I’M BEGGING YOU: stop soaking your dentures in a glass overnight.” Then the signs in customer words (yellow edges, smell by lunch, film you can scrape) and a quiet “I wish I’d switched sooner.”

DenturesTop of funnel

04 Dr. Patricia Sullivan · 48 days running

Raw evidence photo, zero text

A plain phone photo of something gross in an everyday place (a urine cup on a dashboard). The hook lives entirely in the primary text.

DentalPULSE version

Flash photo at night of a soak cup on the edge of the bathroom sink: cloudy water, a brown ring at the waterline, denture inside. Primary text: “This is what my mom’s dentures sat in every night.”

DenturesTop of funnel

05 How Things Break · 127 days running

The gross reveal

A close-up of hidden grime (inside a washing-machine drum) with a warning headline. One of the longest-running statics we found.

DentalPULSE version

Macro of the slimy film ring inside an old denture soak cup, lit like a crime scene: “What’s growing in your soak cup.”

06 Vitaclean · 22 days, rising

Proof you can hold

A hand holds the dirty filter next to a clean one in the shower. The proof is a physical object.

DentalPULSE version

“The tissue test”: a hand holds two tissues, both wiped on the same denture. One has a yellow-brown smear (before), the other is clean (after one 5-minute cycle). The Pod sits on the vanity behind them.

People first, product second

Our ads lead with the Pod. These lead with the person and what changes for them.

Two taped photos of an older couple on their porch. “Before”: she laughs behind her hand. “After”: she laughs with her mouth open. The Pod appears only as a small cut-out at the bottom.

Next step

Tell me which numbers to build (for example “3, 7, 8, 13, 18”) and I’ll render them as a batch. A few notes for when we do:

  • Quotes (13, 15) use real review lines, never invented ones
  • In 5, 11 and 16 the bacteria images are illustrations and will be marked as such
  • No expert personas we can’t back up. 14 uses “Here’s what I recommend” without a name or title
  • Bathroom-only, and nobody holds the Pod
